person.label: Person
person.description: Everyone the timetable places or notifies.
person.keywords: people, staff, student, lecturer, teacher, roster, directory

externalRef.label: External reference
externalRef.help: Stable id from an external SIS or LDAP, used to reconcile imports.

timezone.help: Display and export only. It never affects grid placement or "same day" logic.

roles.label: Scheduling roles
roles.help: What this person can be scheduled AS: Lecturer, Auditor. Not permissions.

accessRoles.label: Access roles
accessRoles.help: What this person may DO in Calendry. Distinct from the scheduling roles above, which are vocabulary and grant nothing.
accessRoles.emptyWarning: No access role assigned. This person can sign in and will be shown an empty application: no schedule, no navigation.

groups.label: Group memberships
groups.help: Which cohorts and seminars this person belongs to.

role.label: Role
role.description: Scheduling vocabulary: Lecturer, Auditor. Not permissions.

key.label: Key
key.help: Stable identifier used by imports and constraints. Cannot be changed later.

room.label: Room
room.description: Physical and virtual spaces sessions can be placed in.
room.keywords: room, space, hall, lab, venue, building, capacity

capacity.label: Capacity
capacity.help: Seats. Leave it 0 for no limit: an online room, or one nobody has measured.

examCapacity.label: Exam capacity
examCapacity.help: Seats available for an exam sitting, if fewer than the normal capacity: exam spacing and invigilation often use more room per person. Leave unset to fall back to this room's normal capacity.

ranking.label: Ranking
ranking.help: Desirability, HIGHER = more premium. The "Steer room choice by rank" constraint reads this to bias placement toward one end of the scale.

equipment.label: Equipment in this room
equipment.help: What this room provides. Offerings requiring it can only be placed here, and a count is what an offering asking for a minimum is measured against. Left blank, this room answers presence only.

equipment.label: Equipment
equipment.description: Feature tags rooms provide and offerings require.
equipment.keywords: equipment, feature, projector, lab, tag, facility

key.label: Key
key.help: Stable identifier used by imports. Cannot be changed later.

group.label: Group
group.keywords: group, cohort, class, section, seminar, nesting, hierarchy, tree

expectedSize.label: Expected size
expectedSize.help: Advisory headcount for room-capacity checks. Membership remains the source of truth.

parentGroupId.label: Parent group
parentGroupId.emptyHint: No other groups to nest under yet.

curriculumPlanId.label: Curriculum plan
curriculumPlanId.help: The plan this group is meant to follow: an intent, set before it has any offerings. Lets the plan’s own "roll out to several groups" panel pre-select this group instead of it being picked by hand every time. Not the same as which plan this group already has offerings from; see the "Curriculum plans" panel below for that.

terms.label: Available in terms
terms.help: Leave empty to make this group available in every term. Adding terms restricts it to those, which is what narrows the group pickers on offerings in other terms.

timeGrid.label: Time grid
timeGrid.description: Block length, blocks per day, and which days this institution teaches on.
timeGrid.keywords: time grid, timegrid, blocks, periods, slots, days, schedule shape

sessionKind.label: Session kind
sessionKind.description: Your own vocabulary: lecture, lab, seminar. Nothing here is built in.
sessionKind.keywords: kind, type, lecture, lab, seminar, exam, vocabulary, category

key.label: Key
key.help: Stable identifier used by imports and constraints. Cannot be changed later.

type.label: What it is
type.help: Decides which rules reach this kind. {examHelp}

color.help: Tints this kind on the schedule. Chips stay legible without it: colour is never the only cue.

requiresGroup.label: Carries groups
requiresGroup.help: Whether sessions of this kind are expected to have Groups assigned. Lets a group-based constraint be rejected when aimed at a kind that has none.

requiresLecturer.label: Needs a lecturer
requiresLecturer.help: Off for a kind such as self-directed study, where an offering with nobody assigned is correct rather than unstaffed. On by default: an offering of a kind that needs one and has nobody assigned is flagged on the next solver run.

offering.label: Offering
offering.description: What must be scheduled: the recurring demand sessions are placed from.
offering.keywords: offering, course, module, subject, demand, curriculum, lecture

color.help: Tints every session of this offering. Leave it empty to inherit the session kind's colour: empty means inherit, not grey.

termId.label: Term
termId.emptyHint: Create a term first: an offering has to belong to one.

kindId.label: Kind
kindId.emptyHint: Create a session kind first: lecture, lab, seminar, whatever you call them.

frequency.label: Sessions per term
frequency.help: Exactly this many sessions must exist. Enforced as a hard constraint.

durationBlocks.label: Length in blocks
durationBlocks.help: How many consecutive TimeGrid blocks one session occupies.

schedulingPattern.label: How the sessions spread
schedulingPattern.help: A weekly slot for the whole term, or the whole course in a short block. Recorded either way; it changes a timetable only once an administrator enables the matching rule.

requiredRoleId.label: Required role
requiredRoleId.help: Scheduling role a lecturer must hold to lead this. Leave unset if it does not matter.

requiredLecturerCount.label: Lecturers needed at once
requiredLecturerCount.help: Leave blank to require exactly one, chosen by the solver from “Who leads it” below. Set higher only for genuine co-teaching: the list below is a candidate pool, not a guaranteed roster.

requiredRoomCount.label: Rooms needed at once
requiredRoomCount.help: One for almost everything. Above one, a session occupies that many rooms simultaneously and their capacities are ADDED: 120 students fit two 60-seat halls. Use it for a cohort too large for any single room, not for a practical where each room must hold everyone. At most {max}.

requiredCapacity.label: Required room capacity
requiredCapacity.help: Leave unset to derive it from the attached groups. Compared against the SUM of the capacities when more than one room is needed at once.

derived.noGroups: No groups attached, so nothing can be derived: every room would qualify.
derived.noSize: The attached groups have neither members nor an expected size, so nothing can be derived: every room would qualify.
derived.line: If left blank: {capacity}, from {count} attached group ({source}). | If left blank: {capacity}, from {count} attached groups ({source}).
derived.warning: Warning: only {capacity} of an expected {estimate} are enrolled, so this may be incomplete.

onlineMode.label: Online delivery
onlineMode.help: Online delivery is a virtual room, not a flag on the session. “Online only” restricts placement to the virtual rooms and is intersected with the room list below if one is set; it also makes the online-related rules (online/on-site same day, maximum online share, concurrent online sessions) materially harder to satisfy.

groups.label: Groups this is for
groups.help: Nesting propagates: assigning a cohort also blocks its seminars. Only groups available in this offering’s term are listed.
groups.emptyHint: No groups available in this term.

lecturers.label: Who leads it
lecturers.help: Eligible to lead it: a candidate pool the solver chooses from, sized by “Lecturers needed at once” above. Optionally state the scheduling role each person fills here.

equipment.label: Equipment it needs
equipment.help: Restricts placement to rooms providing all of it. A count means at least that many units, so only rooms that state enough qualify.

rooms.label: Only these rooms
rooms.help: Restricts placement to exactly these rooms; leave empty for any eligible room. This is not a preference: it is combined with the capacity, equipment and online requirements, so too narrow a list leaves the offering with nowhere to go.

offeringTemplate.label: Offering template
offeringTemplate.description: Reusable offering shapes, such as "Maths, 4x/week", a new offering can start from.
offeringTemplate.keywords: template, offering, shape, reuse, preset, copy

name.label: Template name
name.help: What you pick this template by, not the title it gives the offering.

title.label: Offering title
title.help: Leave blank to name each offering individually.

kindId.label: Kind
kindId.emptyHint: Create a session kind first: lecture, lesson, whatever you call them.

requiredRoleId.label: Required role
requiredRoleId.help: The "lecturer pool" hint. A specific person is named on the offering itself, not here.

lecturers.label: Who leads it
lecturers.help: Named People this template seeds onto every Offering created from it, sized by "Lecturers needed at once" above. Optionally state the scheduling role each person fills. Copied once at apply time — editing this list later does not restaff Offerings already created from the template.
lecturers.emptyHint: No people defined yet. An Offering created from this template will have an empty lecturer pool.

offeringPlan.label: Curriculum plan
offeringPlan.description: A cohort’s whole course load, bundled: apply it to a group to create every offering at once.
offeringPlan.keywords: plan, curriculum, jahrgang, cohort, bundle, template, load

nextPlanId.label: Successor plan
nextPlanId.help: What a Group on this plan moves to next: "Semester 3" names "Semester 4". Lets a Group advance with no picker: the Term defaults to whichever starts next.
nextPlanId.emptyHint: No other plans to point at yet.

constraint.label: Constraint
constraint.description: The rules a timetable must respect, and the preferences it should weigh.
constraint.keywords: constraint, rule, hard, soft, penalty, conflict, policy

screen.label: Screen
screen.description: Lobby and corridor displays showing live room occupancy or today's substitutions.
screen.keywords: screen, screens, display, displays, lobby, kiosk, signage, board, monitor, tv, corridor, occupancy, substitution, substitutions, cover, vertretung, vertretungsplan

name.help: Where the display physically is (e.g. "Main entrance", "B-block corridor"), so the right one can be revoked without a guess.

isActive.help: Turning a screen off stops its key working immediately, and is reversible. Deleting it is not.

mode.label: Board
mode.help: Which board this display draws. A room board shows live occupancy; a substitution plan shows today's and tomorrow's cover, cancellations and moves.

term.label: Term
term.description: Academic periods sessions are scheduled within.
term.keywords: term, semester, trimester, academic, year, period

timeGridId.label: Time grid
timeGridId.help: Which grid this term is scheduled on. Falls back to the tenant default when unset.

calendarPeriod.label: Calendar period
calendarPeriod.description: Holidays, break weeks and exam periods within a term.
calendarPeriod.keywords: calendar, period, holiday, break, exam, vacation, reading week, recess

termId.label: Term
termId.help: Which term this period falls in. Cannot be changed afterwards: moving a period to another term is creating a different period.

kind.label: Kind
kind.help: An EXAM period claims any week it touches. A BREAK or HOLIDAY claims a week only if it covers the whole of it.

account.label: Login
account.description: How people sign in: credentials, separate from the people they act as.
account.keywords: account, accounts, login, logins, credential, password, sign in, signin, user, users, reset

email.label: Email
email.help: The sign-in address, and unique across the whole deployment: one credential can act in several institutions.

mustChangePassword.label: Must choose a new password at first sign-in
mustChangePassword.help: A password an administrator knows is a shared secret. This is what makes that temporary: sign-in succeeds but issues no session until it is changed.

isActive.help: Deactivating blocks sign-in immediately, in every institution this credential is used at. The Person stays on the timetable either way.

accessRole.label: Access role
accessRole.description: Who may do what: bundles of permissions people are granted.
accessRole.keywords: access, permission, role, admin, rights, authorization, security

key.label: Key
key.help: Stable identifier. `create:account --role <key>` and any import address the role by it, so it cannot be changed later.
